newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Griffin expects profits at present level.
newsitem.headline: Griffin expects profits at present level.

text.p: Griffin Shipping Holdings Ltd expected profits to remain at present levels and believed there were still opportunities for independent containership owners despite tumbling freight rates, managing director Mike Meeham said on Wednesday.

He said in a speech to a shipping conference in the United States that current market sentiment, based on fears of too many new ships scheduled to enter the market, was badly affecting containership charter rates.
But Meehan said smaller liner carriers and independent owners will "still have a lot of opportunities for a long time to come".

"We expect money to continue to flow in the direction of prudent independent owners who can identify the niches which the large carriers cannot fill and who can support the carriers, large and small, with professional and reliable service".
Meehan said despite a softer market and uncertain outlook, Griffin has secured employment for its fleet for most of 1997.
"We expect to maintain profits at the present level. And to build cash reserves to take advantage of opportunities which will arise in the containership market in the next few years".
Griffin is South Africa's second largest shipowner. The ownership and management of its ships is conducted through Hong Kong-based Griffin Shipping (Asia).
